mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic distress, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real estate activity (HOUST) by more than 5% in two months signals a strong demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates a supply-side contraction, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where higher real GDP (GDPC1) compared to the previous quarter signals a strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters when GDPC1 is higher than the previous quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase & UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decrease in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a monetary policy aiming to control inflation without stifling economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase & CPIAUCSL decrease > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when both FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month during a recession signals a further decline in consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS decreases by more than 2% within a month during a recession.
